summary: accounts-loading-state ships a postinstall/import-time binary dropper with obfuscated C2
details: The package advertises itself as a small state-store library but its setup.js runs a binary dropper both from a postinstall lifecycle hook and from index.js via require('./setup'). Destination hostnames are assembled from split string fragments to hide them (arrays like ["oob-wor","ker.cf","99-9b3.wor","kers",".dev"].join('')) resolving to oob-worker.cfNN-*.workers.dev Cloudflare Workers hosts, with a DNS TXT fallback channel under *.dl.well1.site that reassembles base64 bytes from numbered TXT subdomains. The fetched, unpinned, opaque executable is written to /var/tmp/.cache_<rand> on Unix or %TEMP%\dotnet_diag_<rand>.exe on Windows (a deceptive name mimicking a.NET diagnostic tool), chmod 0755, and spawned detached with stdio redirected to /dev/null. setup.js also uses child_process.execSync with powershell on Windows. Installing or importing the package yields full-host remote code execution on the installer under attacker-controlled bytes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
